report:
Reviewed the complete meta.reviews.fragment_format claim and its sole ordinary implementation association in crates/sage-meta/src/review.rs, the whole implementation file supplied by start, and the complete sole associated test initial_context_preserves_instructions_and_exact_uniform_fragments. Captured reviews.md and the test fixture definitions (tests/review.rs lines 1-106) through review read. No TODO or not_applicable entries are present or needed.

Requirements: each fragment has a workspace-relative UTF-8 path, a selector, and exact selected contents represented as source lines; joining with newline must restore whitespace and line endings. The Rust model must support WholeFile, inclusive numeric LineRange fields, Claim with anchor_id, and Test with crate_name, target, and rust_path; no particular JSON encoding is mandated. InputFragment has exactly path: String, selector: Selector, contents: Vec<String>. Selector has all four required variants and fields with the specified String/usize types. The chosen tagged serde encoding is permissible and deny_unknown_fields prevents accidental extra fields. inventory constructs claim, whole implementation file, and test fragments in this same representation; capture_read constructs additional fragments using the same type for every selector variant. source_path checks workspace-relative paths and rejects absolute/traversal/escaping paths. source_lines uses split('\n'), not lines(), so carriage returns, spaces, tabs, blank lines, and the final empty component of newline-terminated text are retained. Joining split components with the same separator is exactly reversible, including empty selected text, LF and CRLF text, and text without a trailing newline. select returns strings without representation-stage trimming; claim normalization is the separately specified selection contract.

The associated test visibly checks the stored input deserializes equal to the returned input, then asserts the claim selector identity and relative path with exact reconstructed claim text; locates a WholeFile fragment by its relative source path and asserts reconstructed text equals the actual fixture file; and locates the Test selector and asserts its path and reconstructed contents equal the complete TEST constant. Fixture::input reads persisted input.json directly, so this also covers serialization/deserialization of the fragment model. Fixture source contains a newline-terminated implementation file and an indented, multiline test with attributes and an internal comment and without trailing newline: these assertions catch loss of trailing newline, indentation, comments, or selected source content. All assertions are visible in the associated test body; fixture helpers only prepare files and load JSON. The test also verifies exact instructions/prompt, absence of an unnecessary whole test-file fragment, and association counts/status, which are useful context but not substitutes for the fragment content assertions. The LineRange variant and its usize fields are directly established by the model; detailed selection boundary behavior belongs to the separate selector_line_range claim rather than this representation claim. All model variants use the same contents representation, whose preservation is supported both by the concrete reconstruction assertions and inspection of the lossless split/join implementation.

This is source inspection, not an independent functional test execution. I executed cargo meta review start and review read to capture these inputs; the coordinator separately reports 331 passing sage-meta functional tests, 46 passing sage-stash tests, and a passing workspace build, which I did not rerun. No production or test files were edited. No missing implementation requirement, unjustified placeholder, or actionable test adequacy defect was identified for this representation claim.

Fresh-review assessment: started again using /tmp/sage-refresh-4.txt, consumed the current claim, association metadata and complete test, compared all initial fragments against the previously inspected snapshots, and recaptured every relied-on helper and the review specification. The entire implementation file and claim are byte-for-byte unchanged. The sole associated test adds only a meta.reviews.preparation annotation; its substantive assertions and fixture remain unchanged. This additional association does not weaken or alter any fragment-format coverage. Reassessed each requirement and the actual assertions described above against the new inputs; the same concrete rationale remains supported. No source changes or additional functional tests were performed. This report is freshly recorded by the assigned reviewer, with no requested edits.
